(a) Designation.—The portion of highway US–24 in the State of Michigan, beginning at Interstate 96 and extending north to Interstate 75 at exit 93 west of Clarkston, shall be known and designated as the “Max M. Fisher Memorial Highway”. 
    (b) References.—Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the highway portion referred to in subsection (a) shall be deemed to be a reference to the “Max M. Fisher Memorial Highway”.

fable.w: This section only names a stretch of highway and says existing federal records are deemed to refer to the new name. The tempting reading is that the word "regulation" or the mention of the State of Michigan signals rulemaking or state consultation. But "regulation" appears only in a list of records, and Michigan is only the highway's location. No party outside the federal government is consulted, heard, or given a right to challenge any federal decision.

opus.w: This section only names a stretch of US-24 in Michigan the "Max M. Fisher Memorial Highway" and says how existing references to it should be read. It has no comment period, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation or right to sue. The word "regulation" just appears in a list of documents and does not give anyone power to make rules, so it is not participation.
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through:** Someone might read the word "regulation" in subsection (b) as a grant of rulemaking power. That reading fails. The word only appears in a list of records where references to the highway will be "deemed" to mean the new name. No agency is told it may or must issue rules, and nobody outside the federal government is brought into any decision. The section simply names a road.

qwen_chat.w: This section simply designates a specific portion of a highway with a memorial name. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) in making this decision. The action is unilateral and statutory.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that naming a highway after a person involves some form of public recognition or consultation, but the text itself contains no procedural requirement for outside parties to participate in the decision. The designation is made directly by statute.
